## Problem

`gulliver check --max-change PCT` compares the row count with the previous check of the same target. The history file is keyed by the `connection` **argument**, before it is resolved to a connection name. So the same table on the same connection gets two histories, depending on whether you pass `-c`:

```bash
export GULLIVER_DSN=t.duckdb          # one connection, named "default"
gulliver check t --max-change 5 --json | grep previous_rows   # "previous_rows": 100
gulliver check t -c default --max-change 5 --json | grep previous_rows   # (nothing: no history found)
gulliver check t --max-change 5 --json | grep previous_rows   # "previous_rows": 100
```

The key is `f"{connection}|{source}|{where}"`, so it is `None|t|` in one case and `default|t|` in the other. An agent that sometimes passes `connection` in the MCP `gulliver_check` tool and sometimes not gets a row-count check that silently never compares.

## Where to start

- `src/gulliver/features.py:493-495`: the history key is built from `connection`. Resolve the name first, e.g. `conn_name = settings.connection(connection).name` (this raises `ConfigError` for an unknown name; catch it like the code below does) and use that in the key.
- `src/gulliver/features.py:497-511`: where the history is read and written.
- Optional, nice to have: when the new key has no file but the old `None|...` key does and `connection` was omitted, read the old one, so existing histories keep working.
- Tests: `tests/test_features.py:329` (`test_check_row_count_change`) shows how to run two checks and look at `previous_rows`.

## Done when

- [ ] a check with `connection=None` and one with the default connection's name share one history
- [ ] two different connections still keep separate histories
- [ ] a test covers both
- [ ] `pytest` and `ruff check .` pass
